title: Ex-TSMC CTO says Taiwan's research institutes get too much funding and train too little talent
content: Taiwan directs too much public research and development (R&D) funding to its national research institutes, according to Chenming Hu, a former chief technology officer of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). In his new book, Find the Solutions, Hu argues that this funding does not achieve the same multiplier effect as investment in universities.

title: Transformation in focus as display supply chain kicks off investor briefings
content: The panel display supply chain's transformation marathon continues as companies begin a week of investor briefings centered on new businesses. CoreIntelligence (CiHC), AUO, Radiant, BenQ Materials and E Ink will present in succession, with transformation progress remaining a key market focus.

title: Oracle accelerates AI chip diversification with Cerebras, Google, and SambaNova deals
content: Oracle has signed partnerships with Cerebras and other chipmakers to host their chips in its cloud infrastructure. The Cerebras deal gives the chipmaker a new large customer to anchor its post-IPO trajectory, while allowing Oracle to reduce its reliance on Nvidia's expensive chips, even though Oracle also announced a purchase of Vera Rubin platforms for its data centers.

title: CHPT posts record 3Q26 results as nine-month profit jumps over 90%
content: Chunghwa Precision Test Tech (CHPT), a major semiconductor test interface supplier, posted record revenue and profit in the third quarter of 2026 as consolidated net profit reached NT$551 million (US$16.97 million), up 11.5% quarter on quarter and double the figure from a year earlier. The company has earned more than one times its paid-in capital for three consecutive quarters, with earnings per share reaching NT$16.75.

title: SK Hynix bets on EUV to extend 6F-squared DRAM as CXMT pushes 4F-squared
content: SK Hynix plans to extend the life of its existing 6F-squared DRAM cell architecture through extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography and process improvements, keeping 4F-squared and three-dimensional (3D) DRAM on its technology roadmap as China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) prepares to unveil a product based on a smaller cell design.

title: Cloud AI costs drive demand for on-premises computing, squeezing Asus RTX Spark supply
content: Asus and Intel on October 27 unveiled the new commercial laptop Asus ExpertBook A7 in Taiwan, as on-premises AI computing devices gain attention from enterprises and creators alongside traditional business PCs. Asus said products related to Nvidia RTX Spark, particularly models with 64GB and 128GB of memory, are being allocated due to strong global demand, with the next shipments expected to arrive progressively by the end of October.

title: AI startups face scrutiny over revenue metrics used to promote rapid growth
content: AI startups' revenue figures are under scrutiny as founders and investors question whether companies clearly distinguish active business from contracts that have not yet generated sales. The debate concerns how growth is presented to backers, employees and customers, and whether apparently comparable figures measure the same thing.

title: Kentec targets CSP opportunities with AIDC infrastructure integration
content: Kentec, a subsidiary of Kenmec Group, is shifting beyond its traditional role as a contract manufacturer of components to become a systems integration provider (SIP) for complete AI data center (AIDC) infrastructure. title: PC makers reportedly shift production back to China as AI boom drives up component costs
content: US and Taiwanese PC makers are shifting some production from Southeast Asia back to China and partnering with additional Chinese contract manufacturers as surging memory and storage costs squeeze margins, reversing part of the industry's previous push to diversify supply chains away from China.

title: India-based Spintronics AI weighs GaN chip fab in Madhya Pradesh
content: Hyderabad-based Spintronics AI Semiconductors said on October 27 that it is evaluating the feasibility of establishing a gallium nitride (GaN) semiconductor fabrication facility at Vikram Udyogapuri in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, with a total proposed investment of about INR28 billion (US$294.14 million), according to ETElectronicsWorld. The company works in GaN, RF, and power semiconductor design.

title: AMD to invest US$1 billion in Meta's stock sale as Helios racks enter testing
content: AMD is backing one of its largest AI customers with capital and chips. Alongside an update on its hardware work with Meta, the chipmaker said on October 27 that it will invest US$1 billion in Meta's equity offering, joining Nvidia in buying into the social media company's fundraising for AI infrastructure. Critics describe this pattern as circular financing.

title: SK Hynix's Solidigm ties US$45B US NAND fab to Washington nod on China tool upgrade
content: Solidigm, the US-based subsidiary of SK Hynix, is in talks with the US Department of Commerce over a potential US$45 billion investment in a new NAND flash memory fabrication plant, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the discussions.

title: SK Hynix's next bet goes beyond memory chips
content: SK Hynix is looking beyond its position as a leading supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), using venture investments to gain a greater say in how next-generation AI infrastructure is designed.

title: Fujifilm to boost magnetic tape capacity 5x as AI data storage demand grows
content: Fujifilm will invest JPY10 billion (US$63.3 million) to increase its magnetic tape production capacity 5x by fiscal 2028, in response to rising demand for long-term data storage as artificial intelligence expands global data generation.

title: SK Hynix looks beyond IPO to fund Solidigm's US expansion
content: SK Hynix is reassessing how to finance the US manufacturing expansion of its NAND flash subsidiary Solidigm after shelving a potential initial public offering (IPO), as the South Korean memory maker prepares for higher capital spending in 2027 while committing approximately KRW100 trillion to shareholder returns this year.
